entries.name: Abyssal Beast
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Abyssal Beasts are animals or monsters warped by demonic influence, failed summoning, breach exposure, or abyssal corruption. They are not civilized demons; they are predatory expressions of infernal damage to the natural world.

DESCRIPTION
Use corrupted animal traits: extra eyes, smoking wounds, horn growths, blackened claws, ember veins, twisted jaws, barbed tails, or ash falling from fur or scales.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Abyssal Beasts hunt, guard cult places, spread fear, or signal that a seal is weakening. They fight like animals enhanced by fire, pain, frenzy, or unnatural endurance.

NAMING CONVENTION
Usually descriptive: Ash-Hound, Maw Boar, Cinder Stag, or cult-given names.

entries.name: Abyssal Larva
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Abyssal Larvae are infantile or half-formed demonic life, disgusting signs that a breach or corruption is reproducing.

DESCRIPTION
Pale or charred wormlike bodies, tiny horn buds, too many mouths, and blind hunger for heat or fear.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for horror, contamination evidence, cult nurseries, and early warnings that something worse is coming.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Abyssal Tiefling
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Abyssal Tieflings are tieflings whose bodies or bloodlines have been altered by abyssal corruption, breach exposure, or dangerous infernal forces rather than ordinary demon-blooded ancestry.

DESCRIPTION
Tiefling base with sharper horns, darker markings, ember cracks, unsettling eyes, or other visible signs of supernatural alteration.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use sparingly for cult stories, breach aftermath, infernal contamination, internal conflict, and characters who may be feared for altered ancestry even when innocent.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Academy Familiar
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Academy Familiars are bonded helpers used by students and scholars for lab tasks, note-carrying, detection, or comfort.

DESCRIPTION
Small animals or constructs with ribbons, tags, little satchels, ink stains, or arcane marks showing ownership.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Crownspire and Arcanum scenes, student life, accidents, and clues moving through nonhuman witnesses.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Air Elemental
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Air Elementals are living wind spirits associated with storms, mountain heights, sky islands, and ancient weather magic.

DESCRIPTION
Mostly invisible or translucent bodies of wind, dust, cloud, leaves, feathers, or pressure distortions.

USE IN PLAY
Use Air Elementals for Cloudspire, mountain passes, sky rituals, and weather-based encounters.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Ancient Vampire
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Ancient Vampires are old night-blooded rulers or survivors whose memories and contracts predate many living houses.

DESCRIPTION
Pale, refined, corpse-still figures with old clothing, predatory composure, fangs, cold hands, and a gaze that makes time feel heavy.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use rarely for Nightglass high politics, ancient debts, forbidden bargains, and figures too dangerous to treat as ordinary enemies.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Angel
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Angels are powerful celestial beings tied to judgment, protection, divine command, or ancient holy wars. They should be rare and awe-inspiring, not common temple guards.

DESCRIPTION
Radiant humanoid forms with wings or light-structures, weapon-like halos, impossible symmetry, and expressions that may feel merciful or terrifying.

USE IN PLAY
Use Angels only for major temple mysteries, world-scale oaths, ancient seals, or high religious escalation. Their morality may be strict rather than comforting.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Animated Armor
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Animated Armor is empty armor moved by magic, ghost pressure, bound command, or protective enchantment. It is a guardian type rather than a person.

DESCRIPTION
Suits of armor moving without visible wearer, sometimes with floating weapons, glowing visors, or old heraldry.

USE IN PLAY
Use Animated Armor for castles, training halls, noble vaults, ruins, and magical security encounters.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Arcane Construct
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Arcane Constructs are artificial beings powered by spellwork, cores, runes, relic engines, or bound energy. They may be tools, guards, experiments, or abandoned servants.

DESCRIPTION
Metal, crystal, stone, wood, or composite bodies with visible runes, glowing cores, joint seams, and movements shaped by design rather than biology.

USE IN PLAY
Use Arcane Constructs in Arcanum facilities, ruins, Collegium vaults, celestial-anomaly sites, and old defensive systems.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Arcanum Test Subject
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Arcanum Test Subjects are people or creatures changed by sanctioned or failed magical study. They are a condition-template, not a species.

DESCRIPTION
Base form remains visible under test marks, containment tags, spell scars, altered eyes, or controlled restraints.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for ethical dilemmas, escaped experiments, voluntary study, and people treated as cases by institutions.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Ash Imp
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Ash Imps are smaller, soot-stained imps from burned ruins, failed summons, and Ashen Maw borders.

DESCRIPTION
Tiny horned creatures with gray skin, ember eyes, singed wings, black fingers, and nervous gleeful energy.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for spies, arson pests, cult messengers, bad bargains, and comic-danger scenes around infernal contamination.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Ashbound Mortal
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Ashbound Mortals are people altered by demon-tainted lands, failed summoning, cult rites, or long exposure to infernal corruption. They remain partly themselves, which makes them more tragic than ordinary monsters.

DESCRIPTION
Humanlike or ancestry-appropriate base with ash-gray skin, ember cracks, burnt veins, blackened fingertips, heatless smoke, or eyes reflecting distant fire.

USE IN PLAY
Use Ashbound Mortals as cult victims, corrupted soldiers, failed summoners, desperate pilgrims, or survivors of breach zones, failed summoning sites, or severe infernal contamination. Their condition should suggest danger and loss, not always willing evil.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Ashen Gargoyle
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Ashen Gargoyles are demonic or volcanic variants of gargoyles that perch on infernal ruins and contract courts.

DESCRIPTION
Stone-winged forms with ember cracks, horned faces, ash-scarred claws, and stillness like architecture waiting to judge.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Emberhorn gates, Ashen Maw ruins, and places where law or corruption has become stone.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Astral Construct
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Astral Constructs are artificial forms shaped from Star Arcana, planar residue, or broken transit geometry.

DESCRIPTION
Bodies of blue-white lines, floating plates, transparent limbs, and surfaces filled with shifting constellations.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for celestial-anomaly sites, Arcanum transit failures, Cloudspire ruins, and encounters where space itself has instructions.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Astral Jellyfish
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Astral Jellyfish are floating translucent creatures that drift through air or water around magical thin places.

DESCRIPTION
Bell-shaped translucent bodies, trailing luminous tendrils, and pulsing inner stars.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for magical thin places, Cloudspire, undersea anomalies, and scenes where wonder and danger drift together.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Astral Wraith
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Astral Wraiths are spectral beings touched by stars, void, or broken magical transit. They haunt high places, impact craters, and failed teleportation sites.

DESCRIPTION
Ghostly figures threaded with starlight, dark gaps, drifting motes, and voices that echo as if spoken across distance.

USE IN PLAY
Use Astral Wraiths for celestial-impact mysteries, Arcanum transit failures, Cloudspire ruins, and cosmic horror.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Aurochs Beast
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Aurochs Beasts are enormous wild cattle or monster-bred herd animals dangerous enough to crush fences and armored riders.

DESCRIPTION
Huge horned bovines with scarred hides, heavy shoulders, and earth-shaking charges.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for hunts, steppe hazards, noble sport gone wrong, and rural danger that is not supernatural.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Awakened Animal
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Awakened Animals are ordinary animals granted speech, unusual intelligence, or magical awareness by old forest power, fey influence, druidic rites, or accidents.

DESCRIPTION
They retain animal form but show intelligent gaze, deliberate gestures, chosen adornments, or behavior too purposeful for a normal beast.

USE IN PLAY
Use Awakened Animals for Verdant Expanse diplomacy, strange allies, comic wisdom, local guides, or environmental warnings. Do not make every animal awakened.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Awakened Tree
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Awakened Trees are living trees with awareness but less mobility or personhood than Treants. They speak slowly, remember deeply, and may guard specific places.

DESCRIPTION
Old trees with faces in bark, shifting roots, creaking branches, carved marks grown over, or leaves that turn toward conversation.

USE IN PLAY
Use Awakened Trees for grove guardians, ancient witnesses, hidden paths, and slow environmental conversation.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Badgerfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Badgerfolk Beastkin are compact, stubborn beastkin associated with burrows, defense, endurance, and refusing to move once committed.

DESCRIPTION
Humanlike but sturdy, with badger ears, striped markings, strong hands, heavy shoulders, and grounded stance.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for miners, guards, farmers, tunnel fighters, stubborn elders, and small defenders who become terrifying when cornered.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Banshee
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Banshees are grief-warped spirits tied to death warnings, betrayed women, broken lineages, ruined houses, or places where mourning became a curse.

DESCRIPTION
Pale spectral figures with hair floating like mist, torn formal clothing or burial garments, and a voice that makes air feel thin.

USE IN PLAY
Use Banshees for haunted estates, mourning fields, Nightglass tragedy, and locations where grief is the real danger. They should foreshadow death or reveal emotional truth.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Basilisk
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Basilisks are dangerous reptilian monsters whose gaze, venom, or magical presence can petrify, numb, or paralyze prey depending on local lore.

DESCRIPTION
Low heavy reptile bodies, crown-like head ridges, stone-colored scales, and eyes that characters instinctively avoid meeting.

USE IN PLAY
Use Basilisks for caves, ruined quarries, desert stones, monster forests, and old-road hazards. Their danger should be signaled by statues, stiff corpses, or animals turned unnaturally still.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Bat Swarm
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bat Swarms are dense masses of ordinary or oversized bats capable of becoming dangerous when disturbed, panicked, magically agitated, or trapped in confined spaces.

DESCRIPTION
A churning cloud of wings, claws, teeth, echoes, and sudden direction changes rather than a single targetable creature.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for caves, ruins, towers, abandoned buildings, and underground roads. Their main dangers are confusion, obscured vision, panic, noise, and countless small bites.

NAMING CONVENTION
Usually unnamed and described by location or unusual behavior.

entries.name: Batfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Batfolk Beastkin are nocturnal beastkin with bat ears, sharp hearing, membrane-like features, and strong cave or night instincts.

DESCRIPTION
Humanlike base with bat ears, dark eyes, subtle membrane-like cloak or sleeve styling if desired, fine hearing posture, and clothing adapted for night or caverns. Do not give them full bat wings, animal faces, muzzles, clawed wing-hands, or nonhuman body anatomy.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for cave guides, night messengers, undercity scouts, musicians, spies, and people uncomfortable in harsh daylight.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Battle Familiar
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Battle Familiars are magically bonded creatures trained to support combat without replacing full companions.

DESCRIPTION
Small but fierce beasts, birds, imps, drakes, constructs, or spirits with armor tags, signal ribbons, and alert posture.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for mages, nobles, scouts, and monster trainers. They harry, warn, distract, and deliver small effects rather than dominate combat.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Bearfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bearfolk Beastkin are a powerful beastkin lineage with rounded bear ears, heavy builds, strong arms, thick hair, endurance, and a calm presence that can become terrifying when angered. They are valued as laborers, guards, soldiers, smith assistants, caravan protectors, and mountain guides.

DESCRIPTION
Humanlike base with bear ears, dense build, broad shoulders, and heavy movement. They may have clawlike nails, thick hair, or a deep voice.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Bearfolk often prefer patience, food, family, craft, and directness. In battle they rely on strength, grappling, shields, axes, hammers, and the ability to stay standing under punishment.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use sturdy regional names, mountain names, clan names, or practical frontier names.

entries.name: Bell Wraith
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bell Wraiths are spirits bound to warning bells, plague bells, watch bells, or funeral towers.

DESCRIPTION
Thin spectral forms vibrating with sound, cracked bell metal in the chest, and voices that arrive as ringing pressure.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Blackbell Deadroads towers, plague towns, drowned churches, and hauntings that warn before they kill.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Blink Fox
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Blink Foxes are small magical foxlike creatures able to vanish, reappear, or mislead pursuers through short-range spatial tricks.

DESCRIPTION
Foxes with bright eyes, faint shimmer trails, multiple tail markings, or fur that catches starlight even in shade.

USE IN PLAY
Use Blink Foxes as magical wildlife, omens, familiar candidates, trickster guides, or signs of fey or celestial disturbance.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Blood Knight
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Blood Knights are martial vampires, dhampirs, or blood-bound undead trained for war and court enforcement.

DESCRIPTION
Armored pale figures with red-lined cloaks, elegant weapons, fangs, controlled posture, and armor maintained like noble dress.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Nightglass duelists, vampire house guards, cursed champions, and enemies who fight with discipline rather than frenzy.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Boarkin Beastkin
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Boarkin Beastkin are a beastkin lineage with boar traits, strong builds, tusks or tusk-like teeth, stubborn temperament, and high endurance.

DESCRIPTION
Humanlike build with boar ears, small tusks, coarse hair, powerful shoulders, and grounded stance.

USE IN PLAY
Use Boarkin for farmers, guards, soldiers, clan fighters, and frontier communities where endurance and stubborn loyalty matter.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Bog Beast
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bog Beasts are large swamp monsters made from reptile, boar, bear, or amphibian traits shaped by wetland survival.

DESCRIPTION
Heavy low bodies, mud-caked hide, moss or algae growth, wide jaws, and eyes barely above black water.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Silverfen Marsh, the Drowned Green Coast, and remote marsh roads. They are territorial and hard to track.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Bog Mummy
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bog Mummies are preserved dead from peat, black water, and old sacrifices rather than dry tombs.

DESCRIPTION
Dark leathery bodies, rope marks, peat-stained skin, ritual cuts, and silence that feels older than the marsh.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for ancient marsh sacrifices, drowned rites, and discoveries that force locals to remember what they buried.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Bog Troll
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bog Trolls are swamp-adapted trolls with mud-colored or algae-covered skin, stronger ambush habits, and regeneration fed by wetland conditions.

DESCRIPTION
Large blue-green or mud-dark trolls with long limbs, swamp growth, hooked noses, and bodies that blend into reeds and black water.

USE IN PLAY
Use Bog Trolls for Silverfen Marsh, the Drowned Green Coast, and marsh roads. Fire should remain an important counter.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Bog Witch
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bog Witches are humanoid or semi-human occult figures tied to swamps, black reeds, old bargains, disease lore, herbs, curses, midwifery, river ghosts, and hidden rites. They are not a race in the strict biological sense, but function as a recurring supernatural NPC type in marsh regions.

DESCRIPTION
Describe wet hems, reed charms, bone beads, herb bundles, mossy hair, old hands, strange eyes, or a hut-smoke smell. Some may look harmless until the environment answers them.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Bog Witches bargain, heal, curse, hide fugitives, demand prices, and know old swamp paths. They are best used as morally ambiguous powers, not simple evil hags.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use local names, feared titles, or names tied to reeds, mud, water, crows, or old midwife traditions.

entries.name: Bone Dragon
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bone Dragons are skeletal remains of dragons animated by necromancy, old curse, or lingering draconic will.

DESCRIPTION
Vast dragon skeletons with empty eye sockets, ragged wings, old scale fragments, and necromantic light inside the ribs.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use only for major ruins, late-game undead arcs, and dragon-history horror. They are not ordinary skeletons.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Bone Golem
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bone Golems are necromantic constructs assembled from skeletal material, ritual bindings, grave metal, and death-magic. They are not ghosts but artificial guardians given movement through magic.

DESCRIPTION
Large pale frameworks reinforced with grave metal, armor plates, and visible binding marks. Their shape may resemble an oversized skeleton or an angular funerary statue, and their movement sounds dry and heavy.

USE IN PLAY
Use Bone Golems as necromantic guardians, tomb sentinels, battlefield constructs, or evidence that forbidden magic has disturbed a burial place.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Bone Swarm
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bone Swarms are collections of small bones, fragments, and animal remains animated together by crude necromancy or a lingering curse.

DESCRIPTION
A clattering cloud of pale fragments that flows across floors, climbs obstacles, and briefly gathers into waves, barriers, or grasping shapes before scattering again. Its motion should appear magically coordinated rather than anatomically grotesque.

USE IN PLAY
Use Bone Swarms in catacombs, ossuaries, old burial grounds, and collapsed battlefields. They create eerie environmental danger through numbers, movement, and difficult terrain.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Brass Automaton
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Brass Automatons are clockwork constructs made for service, security, calculation, or ceremonial display.

DESCRIPTION
Brass bodies with gears, glass eyes, ticking joints, polished plates, and movements that repeat designed habits.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Solmire offices, Arcanum labs, gnome workshops, noble estates, and scenes where machinery adds order or unease.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Briar Beast
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Briar Beasts are animal-shaped masses of thorn, root, and old forest anger.

DESCRIPTION
Bestial bodies of tangled briars, wood, leaves, thorns, and glowing eyes hidden in the growth.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Verdant Expanse borders, druidic defenses, abandoned groves, and environmental monsters.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Brimstone Beast
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Brimstone Beasts are demonic animals or war-beasts that carry sulfur heat, smoke, and brutal trained aggression.

DESCRIPTION
Large bestial bodies with horns, smoking jaws, ember veins, cracked hooves or claws, and heat haze around movement.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Ashen Maw patrols, Emberhorn war kennels, cult guards, and creatures that punish panic with pursuit.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Bugbear
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bugbears are large stealthy goblinoids known for ambush, intimidation, and surprising quiet despite their size.

DESCRIPTION
Tall hairy goblinoids with long arms, broad shoulders, sharp teeth, and predatory stillness.

USE IN PLAY
Use Bugbears as ambushers, enforcers, ruin lurkers, and dangerous muscle in goblin or bandit groups.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Bullfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Bullfolk Beastkin are powerful bovine-featured beastkin with horns, broad builds, endurance, and strong protective instincts.

DESCRIPTION
Humanlike bodies with bull horns, ears, tails, thick necks, and heavy-footed presence.

USE IN PLAY
Use Bullfolk for guards, laborers, soldiers, clan protectors, and characters whose size makes others assume simplicity.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Burrower Beast
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Burrower Beasts are large subterranean predators that dig through soil, mine walls, dunes, or old tunnels. They are felt before they are seen.

DESCRIPTION
Heavy bodies with digging claws, armored snouts, poor eyes, and bodies coated in soil, gravel, or mineral dust.

USE IN PLAY
Use Burrower Beasts for mines, desert travel, tunnel collapses, and places where the ground itself becomes unsafe.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Butterflyfolk
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Butterflyfolk are delicate winged humanoids associated with color, transformation, gardens, dream pollen, and social beauty.

DESCRIPTION
Humanoid bodies with butterfly wings, soft antennae, patterned clothing, and gentle movements that can become sudden flight.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for fey courts, garden societies, Dream Arcana, fragile diplomats, and characters whose beauty should not make them powerless.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Catfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Catfolk Beastkin are a feline beastkin lineage with cat ears, tails, sharp senses, quiet steps, expressive eyes, and strong agility. They are common enough to appear in cities, villages, courts, guilds, caravans, and adventuring work, but often face social condescension in noble or bureaucratic settings.

DESCRIPTION
Humanlike facial structure with visible cat ears and tail. Movement should be light, balanced, and observant. Their ears, tail, pupils, and posture should react to emotion.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Catfolk often excel as scouts, messengers, servants, thieves, duelists, dancers, hunters, and agile fighters. They may be underestimated until movement matters.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use names suited to local culture, household service, frontier life, or personal reinvention.

entries.name: Cave Crawler
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Cave Crawlers are large subterranean predators adapted to tunnels, ruins, mines, and deep caverns. Their many limbs and powerful senses allow them to hunt across walls, ceilings, and narrow stone passages.

DESCRIPTION
Long low bodies with many grasping legs, pale or stone-colored hide, sensory feelers, powerful jaws, and little reliance on sight.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for mines, abandoned tunnels, deep roads, cave systems, and underground ruins. They attack from difficult angles, cling to stone, pursue through tight passages, and drag prey away from groups.

NAMING CONVENTION
Usually descriptive names used by miners, delvers, or local communities.

entries.name: Cave Goblin
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Cave Goblins are goblins adapted to darkness, tunnels, fungus farms, and underground scavenging.

DESCRIPTION
Pale or deep-green goblins with large eyes, soot, fungus packs, bone lamps, and tools stolen from miners.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Ironroot lower roads, old mines, and cave lairs where alarms, narrow passages, and hidden pits matter.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Cave Leviathan
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Cave Leviathans are enormous subterranean creatures that inhabit deep roads, underground lakes, or vast caverns. Most surface people think they are legends.

DESCRIPTION
Huge pale or stone-colored bodies, blind eyes, long sensory feelers, and movement that makes caverns tremble.

USE IN PLAY
Use Cave Leviathans as legendary underground hazards, not common monsters. Their presence should reshape routes, clan politics, and mining decisions.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Celestial Spirit
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Celestial Spirits are light-aligned spiritual entities associated with oaths, healing, judgment, mercy, stars, or temple rites. They should feel remote and symbolic rather than casually friendly.

DESCRIPTION
Manifest as figures of light, winged silhouettes, burning script, calm voices, silver eyes, or pressure that makes lies difficult to speak.

USE IN PLAY
Use them for visions, holy sites, old vows, relic reactions, and rare interventions. They should not solve problems cheaply; their presence should create responsibility.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Centaur
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Centaurs are horse-bodied humanoids often associated with plains, old roads, star lore, archery, and clan movement. They may be proud allies or hostile border guardians.

DESCRIPTION
Humanlike torso joined to a horse body, with strong posture, travel gear, weapons, and cultural markings suited to clan or region.

USE IN PLAY
Use Centaurs for steppe clans, ancient roads, ranger allies, mounted culture, and conflicts over territory or respect.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Chimera
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Chimeras are composite magical beasts combining traits from several animals or monsters. They may arise through wild magic, Arcanum experimentation, demon influence, ancient ruins, unusual bloodlines, or natural monster evolution.

DESCRIPTION
Always describe several distinct but integrated creature traits, such as a lionlike body, goatlike horns, a serpent tail, drake scales, wings, unusual eyes, or elemental markings. Chimeras should look clearly supernatural while remaining recognizable as functional living creatures.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Most Chimeras are territorial predators with varied attacks such as bites, claws, tail strikes, breath, venom, flight, or charges. Intelligent Chimeras are rare and should possess motives and behavior appropriate to their origin.

NAMING CONVENTION
Usually descriptive names or experiment labels unless intelligent.

entries.name: Chimera Spawn
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Chimera Spawn are lesser creatures descended from, created alongside, or magically influenced by greater Chimera bloodlines. They combine recognizable animal and monster traits in varied ways.

DESCRIPTION
Their forms may combine goat, lion, serpent, drake, boar, bird, or insect characteristics. Each individual should have a coherent combination of traits suited to its movement, environment, and preferred attacks.

USE IN PLAY
Use Chimera Spawn as magical predators, experimental creatures, unusual offspring, or localized threats around celestial-impact sites, Arcanum facilities, wild-magic regions, and old monster-breeding grounds.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Cinder Devil
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Cinder Devils are mid-tier infernal beings associated with punishment, ash, broken contracts, and fires that consume evidence.

DESCRIPTION
Lean horned figures with burnt parchment skin, coal eyes, long claws, and smoke curling from legal-looking brands.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for contract enforcement, infernal courts, arson coverups, and enemies who destroy proof as a tactic.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Civilized Demon
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Civilized Demons are demon-blooded or true infernal peoples who belong to organized societies such as the Emberhorn Accord. They are not mindless corrupters by default. They may be citizens, judges, soldiers, artisans, merchants, scholars, priests, duelists, diplomats, or nobles bound by law, family, and contract.

DESCRIPTION
Use clear demonic traits: horns, tails, unusual eyes, clawed nails, heat shimmer, dark or red-toned markings, emberlike aura, or infernal elegance. Their clothing should reflect station: court robes, contract chains, volcanic jewelry, military coats, ash-garden silk, or formal armor.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Civilized Demons value binding word, strength, controlled passion, hospitality, debt, honor, and legal precision. They can be intimidating without being evil. Their conflicts should involve pride, treaty, bloodline, contract, exile, or politics rather than random corruption.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use infernal fantasy names with noble house sounds, contract titles, or formal epithets.

entries.name: Clay Golem
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Clay Golems are molded guardians made from earth, clay, prayer, blood, or ritual labor. They are durable and often tied to temples, tombs, or old laboratories.

DESCRIPTION
Heavy clay bodies with cracked surfaces, stamped seals, thick limbs, and impressions of hands or tools left by their makers.

USE IN PLAY
Use Clay Golems for ancient temples, Solarian rites, desert tombs, and old protective magic.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Clockwork Familiar
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Clockwork Familiars are small mechanical assistants made to fetch, scout, record, or assist a mage or inventor.

DESCRIPTION
Tiny brass birds, spiders, cats, mice, or humanoids with winding keys, lens eyes, and delicate joints.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Arcanum scholars, gnome inventors, spies, and utility companions. They are fragile but useful.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Clockwork Gnome
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Clockwork Gnomes are gnomes shaped by mechanism culture, tinkering families, Arcanum workshops, or strange inherited engineering traditions.

DESCRIPTION
Small expressive humanoids with goggles, delicate gloves, spring tools, brass cases, ink stains, and pockets full of parts.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for inventors, academy aides, trap repairers, engine keepers, artificer rivals, and comic but competent experts. They are people first, not jokes.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Cloud Drake
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Cloud Drakes are lesser dragonkin adapted to high altitude, cloudbanks, and sky ruins.

DESCRIPTION
Long pale drake bodies with featherlike fins, light scales, hooked claws, and movements that vanish into mist.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Cloudspire, mountain aeries, and sky-route hazards.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Cloud Giant
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Cloud Giants are true giants associated with high mountains, cloud castles, sky ruins, storm roads, and ancient authority over weather or height.

DESCRIPTION
Enormous humanoids with pale or storm-toned skin, grand clothing, huge hands, and a voice that seems to move through air before sound.

USE IN PLAY
Use Cloud Giants as rare high-tier figures, ancient rulers, skyland nobles, or threats in Cloudspire and northern mountains.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Cloud Ray
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Cloud Rays are manta-like aerial creatures drifting through high winds, sky islands, and cloud seas.

DESCRIPTION
Broad winglike bodies, pale undersides, trailing tendrils, and slow graceful movement through air instead of water.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Cloudspire ecology, sky travel, peaceful wonder, or dangerous herds if startled.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Cockatrice
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Cockatrices are vicious small monsters with birdlike, reptilian, or drake-like features and a cursed bite or gaze that can stiffen flesh.

DESCRIPTION
A nasty hybrid of rooster, lizard, bat, and thorny tail, usually smaller than a human but aggressive beyond reason.

USE IN PLAY
Use Cockatrices as lower-tier but memorable threats in farms, ruins, and monster forests. They work well as pests that become serious when ignored.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Coffin Wight
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Coffin Wights are undead bound to sealed coffins, family crypts, or burial contracts that should not have been opened.

DESCRIPTION
Preserved corpses with splintered coffin wood, burial jewelry, clawed hands, and eyes that open only after trespass.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for crypts, Nightglass secrets, noble tombs, and old burial law. They guard personal guilt as much as treasure.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Comet Hound
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Comet Hounds are magical canines touched by starfall, speed, and night-sky omens.

DESCRIPTION
Lean hounds with silver streaks, bright eyes, light-trailing paws, and coats that flash like meteor dust.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for chases around celestial-impact sites, noble hunts, omens, and companions or predators drawn to magical disturbance.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Comet Stag
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Comet Stags are rare magical deer or elk touched by starfall, moonlight, or ancient sky omens. They are pursued by hunters, scholars, and fools.

DESCRIPTION
Graceful stag bodies with star-speckled coats, antlers like silver branches, and hooves that leave brief sparks or light marks.

USE IN PLAY
Use Comet Stags as omens, guides, sacred prey, or moral tests. Killing one should feel consequential.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Construct
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Constructs are artificial beings made from metal, stone, wood, bone, crystal, or arcane mechanisms. They may be dwarven engines, Arcanum guardians, ancient ruins' defenders, animated armor, golems, or contract-bound machines.

DESCRIPTION
Describe the construction clearly: joints, runes, plates, gears, stone limbs, crystal cores, carved faces, or missing human warmth. They should not bleed or breathe unless designed to mimic life.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Constructs follow commands, guard places, perform labor, enforce trials, or malfunction after centuries. They fight with strength, built-in weapons, armor, and tireless persistence.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use model names, forge names, guardian titles, or names given by caretakers.

entries.name: Contract Devil
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Contract Devils are infernal legalists and pact-beings who treat language, consent, obligation, loopholes, and debt as weapons sharper than blades. They are associated with formal bargains rather than chaotic corruption.

DESCRIPTION
Tall or elegant infernal figures with horns, immaculate clothing, parchment-like skin patterns, burning eyes, or claws stained like ink. They should feel civilized and dangerous.

USE IN PLAY
Use Contract Devils for high-stakes bargains, infernal courts, contested souls, cursed agreements, and Emberhorn legal disputes. They should not attack first if a conversation can trap someone more effectively.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Coral Golem
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Coral Golems are reef constructs or living coral guardians protecting undersea temples and court roads.

DESCRIPTION
Humanoid or beastlike bodies of coral, shell, stone, and reef growth, with fish moving through gaps in their limbs.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Coral Throne defenses, drowned temples, and places where harming the guardian also harms the reef.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Coral Siren
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Coral Sirens are reef-bound sirens associated with coral temples, pearl courts, and songs that shape memory.

DESCRIPTION
Beautiful or eerie aquatic humanoids with coral jewelry, finlike ears, shell ornaments, and voices that seem to echo underwater.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Coral Throne intrigue, undersea romance, dangerous diplomacy, and songs that reveal or conceal truth.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Coral Wraith
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Coral Wraiths are drowned spirits bound to coral growth, wrecks, reefs, or undersea ruins. Their haunting is beautiful and dangerous.

DESCRIPTION
Spectral figures threaded with coral, shells, seaweed, and pale light, often accompanied by drifting sand or bubbles.

USE IN PLAY
Use Coral Wraiths for Coral Throne ruins, shipwrecks, drowned temples, and sea-memory encounters.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Corpse Candle
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Corpse Candles are small ghost-lights or undead flame spirits that appear near graves, marsh deaths, mass burials, or cursed roads.

DESCRIPTION
Floating pale flames, candle-like spirits, or tiny skull-lights hovering over ground where something was buried badly.

USE IN PLAY
Use Corpse Candles as omens, lures, guides, or minor hazards. They should lead toward secrets, traps, graves, or unfinished stories rather than simply attack.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Corpse Leviathan
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Corpse Leviathans are enormous dead beasts, whales, serpents, or giants animated by necromancy or deadland pressure.

DESCRIPTION
Vast undead forms with weathered hide or bone, pale grave lights shining across their frames, and ponderous movement that makes the surrounding terrain feel unnatural.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use rarely for sea horror, dead rivers, plague battlefields, or late-game undead spectacle. Fighting one should be a major event.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Corrupted Mortal
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Corrupted Mortals are people changed by demonic influence, cursed relics, cult rites, or long exposure to corrupted sites, unstable breaches, or failed summoning grounds.

DESCRIPTION
Base ancestry remains visible beneath blackened veins, ember cracks, horn buds, feverish eyes, or ash-stained skin.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for tragic cult victims, failed summoners, altered soldiers, and people whose danger comes from what was done to them as much as what they chose.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Court Familiar
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Court Familiars are magically bonded small creatures used by nobles, mages, witches, or spies in elite households.

DESCRIPTION
Cats, birds, foxes, lizards, tiny drakes, or odd animals with unnatural eyes, jewelry, or behavior too deliberate for pets.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for court intrigue, spying, messages, emotional support, and subtle magical surveillance. They are small but narratively useful.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Crabfolk
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Crabfolk are coastal or reef humanoids with shell plating, clawlike hands, and strong ties to tide pools, reefs, docks, and undersea settlements.

DESCRIPTION
Humanoid bodies with chitin plates, crab claws or clawlike fingers, side-stepping habits, and shell jewelry or coral gear.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Coral Throne citizens, reef guards, dock workers, shellsmiths, and defensive coastal communities.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Craterborn Beast
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Craterborn Beasts are animals or monsters changed by meteoric residue, impact-site magic, or long exposure to impossible minerals.

DESCRIPTION
Retain a recognizable animal or monster shape while adding crystalline patches, luminous markings, unusual coloration, mineral armor, altered senses, or supernatural resilience associated with the impact site.

USE IN PLAY
Use Craterborn Beasts as localized threats around ancient impact sites. Keep them varied but always visibly connected to the strange terrain and magical minerals that changed them.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Crystal Golem
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Crystal Golems are constructs of gemstone, star-crystal, or magical mineral grown into defensive shape.

DESCRIPTION
Humanoid bodies of crystal plates, prism eyes, ringing joints, and light scattered through internal flaws.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for celestial-impact sites, Ironroot mines, Arcanum vaults, and ancient crystal sanctuaries.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Crystal Spider
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Crystal Spiders are cave or celestial-anomaly arachnids with mineral bodies that refract light and magic. They harvest crystal growths, prey, or resonance.

DESCRIPTION
Spider bodies made partly of crystal, glassy legs, prism eyes, and clicking movement like gems striking stone.

USE IN PLAY
Use Crystal Spiders in meteor craters, dwarven mines, crystal caves, and Arcanum research disasters.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Cyclops
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Cyclopes are intelligent one-eyed giant-blooded humanoids found in isolated highlands, mountain valleys, old giant territories, remote islands, ruins, and scattered settled communities. They are smaller than the greatest true giants but considerably larger and stronger than ordinary humans.

DESCRIPTION
Use very large humanoid bodies with a single central eye, heavy bones, broad hands, powerful limbs, and features influenced by local giant ancestry or regional population. Clothing, armor, tools, furniture, and weapons must be built or adapted for their scale.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use Cyclopes as shepherds, smiths, builders, sailors, guards, mercenaries, ruin-keepers, hunters, craftspeople, elders, traders, or members of surviving giant-descended communities. Their size grants reach and strength, but they are not automatically stupid, solitary, primitive, violent, or hostile.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use regional names where Cyclopes live among other peoples. Isolated communities may preserve old giant-influenced personal names, family names, occupational titles, or names tied to mountains, weather, islands, and craft.

entries.name: Dark Elf
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dark Elves are elven peoples shaped by caves, shadowed forests, old exile, underways, or night courts. They are not automatically evil, but often carry histories outsiders distrust.

DESCRIPTION
Pointed ears, graceful but watchful posture, dark-adapted eyes, muted clothing, silver ornaments, underground dyes, or shadow-threaded garments.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for underways, hidden courts, exile politics, Nightglass contact, Arcanum tunnels, and Lythael secrets. Their strength is caution, memory, and precision.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Death Knight
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Death Knights are fallen champions, oathbroken commanders, or cursed paladins bound after death by duty, vengeance, pride, or punishment.

DESCRIPTION
Armored undead figures with preserved martial bearing, old heraldry, dead eyes, and weapons maintained with unnatural discipline.

USE IN PLAY
Use Death Knights for major undead military encounters, old war mysteries, and commanders still following impossible orders. They should have memory and command presence, not just raw aggression.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Deep Dwarf
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Deep Dwarves are dwarven peoples adapted to lower tunnels, sealed roads, old mines, and underground citadels far beneath the surface. They are practical, suspicious, and shaped by darkness more than sunlight.

DESCRIPTION
Short, broad builds like other dwarves, with paler or stone-toned skin, dark-adapted eyes, heavy protective clothing, lamps, masks, and tools suited to deep work.

USE IN PLAY
Use Deep Dwarves for Ironroot lower roads, sealed delvings, undercity trade, old warnings, and conflicts between surface diplomacy and underground survival.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Deep Gnome
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Deep Gnomes are small underground gnomes shaped by tunnels, hidden workshops, crystal caves, and cautious survival beneath larger powers.

DESCRIPTION
Small light builds with large dark-adapted eyes, pale or stone-toned skin, tool belts, lamps, lenses, and quiet practical movement.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Ironroot lower roads, Arcanum underlabs, secret mines, and hidden enclaves. They solve problems through craft, caution, and silence.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Deep One
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Deep Ones are ancient aquatic humanoids from abyssal waters, old sea temples, or forgotten pacts beneath the waves. They are alien, patient, and unsettling.

DESCRIPTION
Fishlike or amphibious humanoids with slick skin, lidless eyes, gills, webbed limbs, and jewelry or carvings from deep cultures.

USE IN PLAY
Use Deep Ones for sea horror, old pacts, undersea politics, and coastal villages with strange bargains. They should feel organized but not easily understood.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Deerfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Deerfolk Beastkin are a graceful beastkin lineage with deer ears, antlers in some individuals, strong hearing, and woodland instincts.

DESCRIPTION
Humanlike bodies with deer ears, soft eyes, possible antlers, light steps, and clothing that may reflect forest, village, or court upbringing.

USE IN PLAY
Use Deerfolk for scouts, herbalists, temple attendants, forest communities, and characters whose gentleness does not mean weakness.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Demon-Touched Beastkin
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Demon-Touched Beastkin are beastkin whose lineage or body has been altered by infernal exposure, cursed breeding, old pact magic, or abyssal corruption. They are feared because ordinary animal traits become sharper, hotter, or stranger.

DESCRIPTION
Base kemonomimi beastkin features remain visible, with fully humanlike face and body. Horns, ember eyes, spade tails, heated clawlike nails, ash markings, or unnatural aggression may overlay the original lineage. Do not turn them into animal-headed demons, furry monsters, paw-handed creatures, or full anthropomorphic animals.

USE IN PLAY
Use this type for borderlands, demon raids, corruption arcs, and tragic transformations. They should not replace normal Beastkin; they show what corruption or infernal pressure can do to a living people.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Demonblood
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Demonblood are mortal people with visible infernal ancestry, often descended from ancient contracts, mixed bloodlines, old pacts, or distant Emberhorn Accord families. They may have horns, tails, ember-bright eyes, unusual heat tolerance, or faintly ritualized instincts around oath and debt. They are not automatically corrupt or evil.

DESCRIPTION
Usually humanlike in build with one or more infernal traits: small horns, swept horns, tails, unusual pupils, warm-toned markings, sharper teeth, or heat-shimmer around strong emotion. Clothing should reflect local culture rather than defaulting to cult robes.

USE IN PLAY
Use Demonblood for social NPCs with infernal heritage who are not full demons or tieflings, especially in Emberhorn, border courts, mixed households, mercenary companies, and foreign embassies. Their conflict should often come from prejudice, contract expectations, family history, or political suspicion.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Demonblood Commoner
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Demonblood Commoners are mortal people with visible infernal ancestry who live ordinary lives in Emberhorn, border towns, mixed households, armies, workshops, farms, ports, and servant quarters. They are not automatically corrupt or evil.

DESCRIPTION
Humanlike or ancestry-appropriate build with small horns, ember eyes, warm markings, tails, sharp teeth, or ritual jewelry worn cautiously or proudly.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for ordinary infernal-blooded citizens, workers, soldiers, servants, apprentices, traders, and refugees. Their drama often comes from prejudice, family expectation, contract culture, and proving they are more than a superstition.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Demonblood Noble
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Demonblood Nobles are mortal or near-mortal infernal-blooded aristocrats, usually tied to Emberhorn houses, old contracts, diplomatic marriages, or families whose bloodline carries visible authority.

DESCRIPTION
Elegant humanoids with refined horns, formal tails, emberlike eyes, volcanic jewelry, contract chains, court robes, or controlled heat around strong emotion.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for demon-court politics, infernal diplomacy, contract disputes, proud heirs, house rivals, and characters who wield etiquette and bloodline as weapons. They should be dangerous socially before physically.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Desire Demon
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Desire Demons are infernal beings that weaponize longing, shame, admiration, loneliness, ambition, or romantic fantasy.

DESCRIPTION
Beautiful or shifting demonic forms with horns, perfect smiles, impossible eyes, perfume-like heat, and details tailored to the target.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for temptation, court corruption, forbidden bargains, and social danger. They should not reduce every scene to lust; desire includes power, praise, safety, revenge, and belonging.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Dhampir
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dhampirs are half-vampiric or vampire-touched humanoids, often born from bloodline pacts, forbidden unions, curses, or controlled Nightglass arrangements. They are living enough to walk among mortals but carry signs of night-blood: hunger, pale eyes, sharpened teeth, cold pulse, or heightened senses.

DESCRIPTION
Dhampirs should look mostly humanoid with subtle vampire traits such as faint fangs, cool skin, red-tinted eyes, unusual stillness, or discomfort around bright rites. They should not automatically look monstrous.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Dhampirs can become hunters, spies, courtiers, outcasts, heirs, assassins, or mediators between mortal and vampire societies. Their drama lies in inheritance, control, hunger, and whether others trust them.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use names from mortal culture or Nightglass-style noble names depending on upbringing.

entries.name: Dhampir Noble
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dhampir Nobles are half-vampiric or bloodline-touched aristocrats raised within courtly night society or among families hiding old vampire ties. They are more socially dangerous than visibly monstrous.

DESCRIPTION
Pale or refined humanoid appearance, subtle fangs, cold elegance, unusual stillness, intense gaze, and clothing shaped by wealth, lineage, or secrecy.

USE IN PLAY
Use Dhampir Nobles for Nightglass politics, secret heirs, courtship and intrigue, bloodline disputes, and characters caught between mortal law and vampire etiquette. They should have restraint, hunger, and social pressure.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Dire Wolf
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dire Wolves are oversized predatory wolves with unusual endurance, pack coordination, and territorial intelligence. Some are natural; others are shaped by magic, old forest pacts, or monster regions.

DESCRIPTION
Huge wolves with heavy shoulders, scarred muzzles, intense eyes, and movement coordinated enough to feel tactical.

USE IN PLAY
Use Dire Wolves for frontier danger, ranger reports, monster forests, winter roads, and beastkin-adjacent stories. They work best in packs with terrain advantage.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names that fit the individual's culture, station, region, and social role.

entries.name: Dissonant Bombard
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dissonant Bombards are unstable manifestations in which trapped emotional-magical pressure has become physically overcharged. They repeatedly build and release dangerous bursts of accumulated energy.

DESCRIPTION
Rounded or compressed manifestations surrounded by colorful shells, masklike faces, trembling outlines, bright fault-lines, and visible surges of unstable light or magical pressure.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use Bombards as clearly telegraphed explosive threats. They build toward dangerous releases, throw unstable magical globes, expand their surrounding aura before detonation, or discharge stored pressure when sufficiently destabilized. Dangerous explosions must always be signaled clearly enough for movement, interruption, separation, or deliberate triggering to matter. Piercing the pressurized manifested shell can destabilize them quickly, though doing so at close range may remain dangerous.

NAMING CONVENTION
Bombard, Burstling, Anger Bomb, Pressure Wretch, and similar names are common.

entries.name: Dissonant Bully
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dissonant Bullies are large manifestations associated with intimidation, resentment, humiliation, dominance, fear turned outward, and repeated emotional pressure between stronger and weaker people.

DESCRIPTION
Heavy brightly colored bodies with oversized shoulders, thick limbs, tiny masklike faces, broad hands, and exaggerated threatening posture. Smaller Dissonants often cluster around or behind them.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use Bullies as heavy control enemies. They shove smaller Dissonants toward opponents, grab characters, block routes, throw victims, slam obstacles, and attempt to dominate space through physical presence. They withstand ordinary impact and Psychic pressure well, but force attacks disrupt the unstable magical mass holding their exaggerated bodies together.

NAMING CONVENTION
Bully, Brute, Shameback, Big Temper, and similar names are common.

entries.name: Dissonant Hexer
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dissonant Hexers form around unstable magical residue, repeated conflict, cursed places, hostile enchantment, failed magical interrogation, or rituals that leave persistent psychic and arcane distortion.

DESCRIPTION
Thin vividly patterned bodies with floating masks, long fingers, many expressive symbols, and visible waves of color, heat, distortion, or trembling light moving around them.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use Hexers as disruption-casters for other Dissonants. They interfere with concentration, clarity, coordination, spell control, and sensory certainty rather than controlling emotions or decisions. Their influence weakens when victims leave the contaminated area, regain stable footing and focus, or disrupt the magical source. They resist Psychic and Arcane effects but are vulnerable to radiant power that imposes clarity and destabilizes their distortion.

NAMING CONVENTION
Hexer, Mood-Witch, Dissonant Whisperer, Bitter Seer, and similar names are common.

entries.name: Dissonant Scrapper
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dissonant Scrappers are aggressive close-combat manifestations associated with frustration, anger, resentment, repeated conflict, and emotional pressure forced into physical action by unstable magic.

DESCRIPTION
Compact brightly marked bodies with oversized fists, hornlike projections, clenched mask-faces, thick forearms, and abrupt jerking movement. Their bodies often appear permanently tensed for another strike.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use Scrappers as relentless melee attackers. They rush targets, interrupt actions, throw repeated combinations, kick obstacles aside, chase anyone who retreats, and become increasingly aggressive when resisted. They endure emotional and blunt pressure well but lack the defensive patience and tactical discipline of trained fighters.

NAMING CONVENTION
Scrapper, Temperling, Red-Fist, Hothead, and similar local names are common.

entries.name: Dissonant Spinner
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dissonant Spinners embody agitation, panic, restless energy, overstimulation, and emotional pressure that cannot settle into a stable direction.

DESCRIPTION
Round or narrow brightly colored creatures with rotating limbs, masks, ribbons, blades, fins, or other exaggerated extensions that accelerate as their agitation increases.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use Spinners as high-mobility disruption enemies. They cross battlefields rapidly, create sweeping attacks, knock combatants out of position, rebound from terrain, and become harder to control as they gain momentum. After a major spin or charge they should briefly become vulnerable, and concentrated force is particularly effective at breaking their unstable rotational cohesion.

NAMING CONVENTION
Spinner, Whirl, Panic Wheel, Rattlewheel, and similar movement-based names are common.

entries.name: Dissonant Spitter
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dissonant Spitters are ranged manifestations frequently associated with contempt, spite, disgust, suspicion, resentment, and hostility that has been repeatedly suppressed or magically amplified.

DESCRIPTION
Lean brightly colored creatures with masklike faces, swollen throats or chest sacs, long arms, narrow bodies, and exaggerated recoiling posture. Their mouths or facial openings distort immediately before launching attacks.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use Spitters behind other Dissonants. They launch acidic, poisonous, irritating, sticky, or magically disruptive projectiles appropriate to the outbreak and environment, then retreat when approached. Their manifested physiology is resistant to poison and Psychic pressure but they perform poorly when forced into sustained melee.

NAMING CONVENTION
Spitter, Spite-Slinger, Bittermouth, Sourling, and similar hostile nicknames are common.

entries.name: Dissonant Titan
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dissonant Titans are rare massive manifestations produced when a severe emotional-magical outbreak becomes concentrated around a powerful magical source, catastrophe, artifact, ritual chamber, experiment, or deliberately constructed Dissonance Core.

DESCRIPTION
Huge exaggerated bodies combining several emotional motifs, shifting colors, cracked masks, oversized limbs, and waves of visible magical distortion. Their posture, coloration, and proportions may change as different emotions dominate the outbreak.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use Dissonant Titans as outbreak bosses. Their behaviour shifts according to dominant emotional pressure: rage creates charges and relentless attacks, fear produces evasive bursts or frantic defenses, grief creates slowing or clinging pressure, shame conceals weak points, and frustration creates increasingly reckless attacks. They resist Psychic pressure and heavy impacts. Destroying the Titan ends the immediate threat but does not automatically remove the magical source or circumstances that created the outbreak.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use Dissonant Titan, Great Dissonant, or a unique title based on the incident, location, dominant emotion, or people affected.

entries.name: Dissonant Wretch
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dissonant Wretches are the smallest manifestations produced when intense negative emotion becomes trapped, amplified, extracted, reflected, or repeatedly fed through unstable magic. Ordinary sadness, anger, fear, shame, or frustration does not create them without an enabling magical disturbance.

DESCRIPTION
Small vividly colored creatures with distorted masklike faces, exaggerated eyes or mouths, uneven limbs, and bodies that pulse, shake, shrink, stretch, or swell according to their dominant emotional pressure.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use Dissonant Wretches in groups as erratic low-level enemies. They hesitate, rush, scatter, regroup, flinch, lash out, and react dramatically to pressure rather than following disciplined tactics. Psychic attacks interact poorly with creatures already made from emotional-magical turbulence.

NAMING CONVENTION
Wretch is the scholarly category. Local names are usually frightened or insulting descriptions based on color, sound, expression, or behaviour.

entries.name: Djinn
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Djinn are powerful air, storm, or desert spirits associated with wind, freedom, old bargains, and impossible travel.

DESCRIPTION
Tall radiant or wind-wrapped figures with flowing garments, storm eyes, floating hair, and bodies partly made of moving air or sand.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for desert courts, ancient lamps, sky bargains, and beings who value freedom enough to make captivity catastrophic.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Dogfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dogfolk Beastkin are a canine beastkin lineage with dog ears, tails, keen hearing, strong scent, and a reputation for loyalty, attentiveness, and practical reliability. This reputation can help them find work but also causes nobles and officers to stereotype them as servants or soldiers.

DESCRIPTION
Humanlike facial structure with visible dog ears and tail. Expressive posture, alert attention, scent-testing, and ear movement should appear in description.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Dogfolk are often scouts, messengers, guards, assistants, patrol soldiers, searchers, and frontier companions. They are good at tracking, warning others, and staying focused under stress.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use local names shaped by service households, military culture, village life, or personal bonds.

entries.name: Doll Construct
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Doll Constructs are small humanoid constructs built from porcelain, cloth, wood, wax, or clockwork for service, spying, or haunting.

DESCRIPTION
Child-sized or smaller doll bodies with painted faces, glass eyes, stitched joints, and movements too deliberate for toys.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for haunted estates, laboratories, noble nurseries, witch huts, and unsettling helpers or traps.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Doppelganger
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Doppelgangers are rare humanoid shapeshifters capable of assuming the outward appearance of other people. Their origins are uncertain and may differ between individuals or lineages.

DESCRIPTION
Their natural forms are pale, smooth-featured, or subtly unfinished humanoids, but most are encountered while imitating another person. Physical imitation does not automatically grant memories, skills, magical abilities, relationships, or knowledge.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use Doppelgangers for infiltration, espionage, identity mysteries, criminal work, survival among hostile societies, and political intrigue. They may be enemies, neutral actors, frightened fugitives, professional spies, or complicated allies rather than universally malicious impostors.

NAMING CONVENTION
They may use personal names, inherited names, aliases, or the identities under which they currently live.

entries.name: Dracolich
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dracoliches are undead dragons that preserved mind and power through forbidden rites. They should be rare, mythic, and campaign-shaping.

DESCRIPTION
Ancient skeletal or mummified dragon bodies with cold arcane fire, cracked horns, dead wings, and intelligence burning in empty eyes.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use only for story-gated threats, forbidden dragon lore, and conflicts where death did not end ambition.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Draconic Scion
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Draconic Scions are rare humanoids whose blood, oath, or soul has been marked by a specific dragon or draconic pact. They are more story-facing than ordinary Dragonkin.

DESCRIPTION
Humanoid base with elemental marks: ember veins, stone-dark scales, water-bright eyes, wind-pale hair, horn buds, or a voice with faint resonance.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use sparingly for pact heirs, dragon-linked NPCs, ancient tests, and bloodline attention. Their importance must be earned through authored story context, not assumed from type alone.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Dragon
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dragons are mighty ageless creatures tied to elemental power, ancient territory, and history older than many kingdoms. Fire dragons are usually red and breathe fire; earth dragons are often black, mountain-bound, peaceful unless provoked, and able to fly or burrow; water dragons are blue, territorial, and tied to oceans, rivers, or deep waters; air dragons are white, nomadic, and often more approachable than other dragons. Age greatly increases power.

DESCRIPTION
Always describe dragons as vast, nonhuman, and majestic: scales, wings, claws, horns, long neck, elemental aura, and a presence that changes the environment. Young dragons are still dangerous; ancient dragons should feel like living natural disasters or sovereign powers.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Dragons should not appear casually. They may be neutral, territorial, friendly, anciently bound, sleeping, watching, or politically significant. They fight with breath, claws, wings, tail, elemental force, fear, and overwhelming endurance.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use ancient titles, elemental epithets, or names that sound older than kingdoms.

entries.name: Dragon (Spiritual Entity)
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
A dragon spirit is the lingering soul, echo, memory, or bound consciousness of an ancient dragon. It should never appear casually. It acts through dreams, relics, ruins, omens, old pacts, pressure in stone, elemental changes, or rare manifestations unless directly awakened by major story events.

DESCRIPTION
Manifestations may appear as burning eyes in darkness, ash-like mist, a vast shadow, a voice in stone, a spectral dragon outline, cold pressure around relics, or ancient language carried by wind or flame.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Dragon spirits should be mysterious and dangerous even when not hostile. They may test bloodlines, recall ancient pacts, haunt territory, guard seals, or tempt ambitious mortals. Direct confrontation should be rare and story-gated.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use ancient titles, elemental names, or epithets rather than ordinary names.

entries.name: Dragonblood Mortal
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dragonblood Mortals carry distant draconic ancestry, pact residue, or bloodline reaction without being dragons. They are rare enough to draw attention if obvious.

DESCRIPTION
Mostly humanoid with subtle scale patterns, slit pupils, heatless pressure, unusual eye colors, faint horns, or elemental reactions under stress.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for rare bloodline mysteries, pact history, noble suspicion, academy interest, and characters who may be watched before they understand why. Do not make them automatically chosen or powerful.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Dragonflyfolk
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dragonflyfolk are winged insectoid humanoids tied to wetlands, river edges, and fast aerial movement.

DESCRIPTION
Light humanoid bodies with iridescent wings, large eyes, quick movements, and clothing that leaves wings free.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for marsh scouts, river couriers, messengers, and fragile-looking characters whose speed controls the scene.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Dragonfolk
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dragonfolk are full-sized draconic humanoid people with clearly nonhuman dragonlike anatomy. They are mortal people rather than lesser dragons and may belong to any realm, culture, profession, faith, social class, or political allegiance. They are distinct from humanlike Dragonkin, natural Lizardfolk, kobolds, drakes, and true dragons.

DESCRIPTION
Dragonfolk have upright humanoid bodies with full scales, distinctly draconic heads and snouts, horns, tails, claws, and powerful humanoid proportions. Their scale colors, horn shapes, facial structures, and builds vary widely. They have two arms and two legs and remain compatible with ordinary humanoid clothing, armor, weapons, and equipment with practical tailoring around horns and tails. Wings are not a standard Dragonfolk trait and should only appear when explicitly established.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use Dragonfolk as ordinary citizens, soldiers, craftspeople, merchants, scholars, priests, adventurers, nobles, diplomats, laborers, guards, or members of older draconic communities. Their scales and strong builds make them physically resilient, but they do not automatically possess breath weapons, elemental powers, magical armor, or the authority of true dragons.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use names shaped primarily by the culture and region where the Dragonfolk was raised. Isolated or old draconic communities may preserve ancient draconic names, lineage names, or translated ancestral titles.

entries.name: Dragonkin
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dragonkin are a stable mortal people with humanlike faces and bodies combined with visible draconic traits. They occupy a different physical niche from Dragonfolk: a Dragonkin should look like a human with dragon features, never like a humanoid dragon. They may belong to any realm, culture, profession, faith, social class, or political allegiance.

DESCRIPTION
Dragonkin retain fully humanlike facial structure, skin, hands, feet, legs, and general body proportions. Their defining draconic traits normally include horns, a scaled tail, and a pair of draconic wings, with possible slit pupils, small scale patches, unusual eye colors, or subtly sharpened teeth and nails. Do not give Dragonkin draconic heads, reptilian muzzles, full-body scales, digitigrade monster legs, animal paws, or Dragonfolk anatomy. Clothing and armor use ordinary humanoid construction with practical openings or fittings for wings, tail, and horns.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use Dragonkin in the same full range of social roles as humans and other settled peoples. Their wings improve balance, controlled descent, gliding, and aerial movement where space and load permit; strong sustained flight depends on the individual's physique, training, equipment, and explicitly established capabilities. Dragonkin do not automatically possess breath weapons or elemental magic.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use names appropriate to the culture and region in which the Dragonkin was raised. Families preserving old draconic lineage traditions may retain ancestral draconic names or secondary lineage names.

entries.name: Drake
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Drakes are lesser dragonkin: powerful reptilian beasts with scales, claws, fangs, and elemental hints, but usually without the full intelligence, age, wings, or authority of true dragons. They may be mountain predators, war beasts, cave guardians, desert hunters, or young offshoots of dragon territory.

DESCRIPTION
Describe scales, heavy bodies, claws, fangs, horns, reptilian eyes, and elemental coloration. Some drakes have vestigial wings or breath-like heat, but they are not true dragons unless specified.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Drakes act more like dangerous beasts than ancient rulers. They guard territory, hunt, bond with rare handlers, or serve as elite mounts and war-beasts. They fight with bites, claws, tail strikes, charges, and armored hides.

NAMING CONVENTION
Usually named by handlers or described by color, lair, or trait.

entries.name: Dreadmark Chain Beast
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Dreadmark Chain Beasts are state-bred or captured monsters controlled by chains, handlers, pain, and military discipline.

DESCRIPTION
Huge scarred beasts with iron collars, chain harnesses, clipped horns or claws, and eyes trained to fear commands.

SOCIAL / COMBAT USE
Use for Dreadmark war scenes, state patrols, border terror, and moral conflict around weaponized creatures.

NAMING CONVENTION
Use fantasy names shaped by the creature type, region, culture, rank, and social role.

entries.name: Drowned Dead
entries.summary:
GENERAL INFORMATION
Drowned Dead are waterlogged undead tied to floods, shipwrecks, river sacrifices, sea battles, or bodies hidden in marsh and harbor water.

DESCRIPTION
